outcome_detail: San Diego County paid more than $9.5 million in total to settle 21 lawsuits brought by women who accused ex-deputy Richard Fischer of sexual assault, with the final three settlements (including two of more than $1 million each) reached around August 2023 after more than five years of litigation. The county separately paid about $1 million to private attorneys defending Fischer in the civil cases.
criminal_detail: In September 2019 Fischer pleaded guilty to four felony counts of assault under color of authority, two misdemeanor counts of assault under color of authority, and one misdemeanor count of false imprisonment, stemming from attacks on 16 women; he was sentenced in December 2019 to 44 months in county jail. He was released in May 2020 after an erroneous award of 956 days of pre-trial home-detention credit, ordered back into custody after a September 2022 appellate ruling, and released again in August 2023 with electronic monitoring.
description: Twenty-one lawsuits were filed against San Diego County and former sheriff's deputy Richard Fischer by women who alleged he groped, fondled, and sexually assaulted them while in uniform and on duty, largely during traffic stops and calls for service in North and East San Diego County between 2015 and 2017. Fischer pleaded guilty in 2019 to seven charges, including four felony counts of assault under color of authority, and was sentenced to 44 months in jail. The county ultimately paid more than $9.5 million to settle the 21 suits, with the final settlements reached in 2023. Reporting on the payouts describes the settlements in aggregate rather than by individual filing.
notes: Aggregate reporting: coverage documents the 21 suits and the $9.5 million-plus total collectively, without separately documenting each individual filing, so this is kept as one record with multiple_filings=true and filing_year_range 2017-2023.
